fix: destroy tcp/unix sockets after checks

The tcp and socket resource checks called conn.end() on success and on
timeout. end() only half-closes the socket; a still-connecting socket
that times out is left un-destroyed, leaking its TCPSocketWrap handle.
Use conn.destroy() so both checks fully release their connections.

Adds api tests for #82: the server sees the tcp/unix connection closed
after a successful check, and a timed-out tcp attempt leaves no leftover
TCPSocketWrap in process.getActiveResourcesInfo() (asserted directly,
since mocha --exit would otherwise mask the leaked handle).

Addresses jeffbski/wait-on#82

ci: semantic-release with approval gate, commitlint and PR-title lint

Add release automation modeled on semantic-release's own release.yml:

- release.yml (push to master): validate -> dry-run preview -> gated
  release, chained with needs: so a red commit never reaches approval.
  Publish gated by the `release` GitHub Environment; remove its required
  reviewers to go fully automatic (no code change). npm OIDC trusted
  publishing + provenance, no stored token. Version committed back with
  @semantic-release/git. Repo-guarded so forks never publish.
- commitlint.yml (pull_request): lint commit messages against Conventional
  Commits, CI only (no husky). Ignores three in-flight contributor
  subjects so PRs #228/#233/#235 stay green (remove once merged).

- package.json: normalize repository.url to https so provenance matches.
- .npmignore: keep release/lint config and docs out of the npm tarball.
- .github/RELEASING.md: how to approve, go autonomous, set up the trusted

All actions pinned by SHA. Tools run via pinned npx (no new devDeps, no

feat(command): serialize execs and add per-attempt commandTimeout

The rebased command: resource (from upstream #88) ran one exec per poll tick
with no upper bound, so a command slower than the interval stacked up and a hung
command wedged the poll loop forever.

- exhaustMap replaces mergeMap(simultaneous): exactly one exec is in flight per
  command resource, regardless of the simultaneous option, so a slow command is
  never spawned concurrently with itself.
- a new commandTimeout option kills a command still running at the per-attempt
  bound (SIGKILL) so polling continues; default 0 keeps the unbounded behaviour.

test(command): cover concurrency, per-attempt kill, and reverse mode

Replace the rebased command tests (which used jest-style matchers under a
chai/mocha suite) with scenarios matching U11:

- command exits 0 succeeds; a persistently failing command polls to timeout
- a failing command that later passes succeeds
- a slow command never runs concurrently with itself (asserts max in-flight is 1)
- a command exceeding commandTimeout is killed and polling continues
- reverse mode waits until the command starts failing

Real-timer polling with short interval/timeout and node child processes, as the
rest of the suite does; no wall-clock date dependence.

installed @types/wait-on@5.3.4. The bundled types were stricter and broke
existing consumers (jeffbski/wait-on#250):

- the callback typed (err: Error | null) rejected (err?: Error) handlers (TS2345)
- the AxiosProxyConfig / HttpSignature type names were removed (TS2694)
- WaitOnOptions dropped TLS options beyond ca/cert/key/passphrase

Relax the declarations back to the @types shape and add regression tests that
would have caught the break. Verified against the runtime: on success the
callback is invoked with undefined (never null); on failure with an Error.

- index.d.ts: cb (err?: Error); WaitOnOptions extends full SecureContextOptions
  (only ca/cert/key/passphrase are read at runtime); deprecated aliases
  AxiosProxyConfig = WaitOnProxyOptions and HttpSignature.
- test/types.test-d.ts: annotated-callback cases plus a @ts-expect-error proving
  null handling is not forced.
- test/types-compat/dt-wait-on-tests.ts: vendored DefinitelyTyped consumer test,
  compiled by test:types so @types consumers stay unbroken.
- test/api.mocha.js: runtime/type agreement test (err === undefined on success,
  including reverse mode).

refactor!: replace axios with native fetch and undici (Node >=22.19)

Remove axios in favor of Node's native fetch backed by an undici dispatcher.
Engines rise to >=22.19 and the CI matrix moves to 22/24/26 (keeping the
Windows row), starting the 10.0.0 train.

- Rebased onto feat/command-resource; reconciles with U3's HTTP_UNIX_RE
  (Windows named-pipe aware, with the legacy form as fallback) and U4's URL
  validation, which still fires before any fetch.
- Per-request undici dispatcher (buildDispatcher): TLS client options and the
  unix socketPath ride on connect; a socketPath always uses a plain Agent, an
  object proxy wraps in ProxyAgent, unset uses EnvHttpProxyAgent, false uses a
  plain Agent.
- fetch is imported from undici rather than the global, so fetch and the
  dispatcher stay on the same undici version across Node majors (Node 22 bundles
  undici 6, Node 26 bundles 8) instead of failing on the mismatch.
- Consume the response body under the request's AbortSignal to preserve axios
  GET timeout parity; abort in-flight requests on teardown.
- index.d.ts proxy docs and README note the >=22.19 floor.

Parity coverage (TLS client options, proxy object/false/NO_PROXY, unix-socket
short and absolute forms) lives in test/https-proxy.mocha.js.

Green: npm test on Node 22.19 and Node 26 (144 passing each).

BREAKING CHANGE: Node >=22.19 is now required (engines floor raised from
>=20.0.0). HTTP checks use Node's native fetch with an undici dispatcher
instead of axios, so axios-specific behavior no longer applies.

test: fix flaky Windows https-proxy before-hook timeout

The `https/tls and proxy parity` before hook shelled out to
`openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 ...` under the suite's tight
`this.timeout(6000)`. RSA-2048 keygen is slow and highly variable on
Windows CI runners and intermittently exceeded 6000ms, timing out the
before hook and failing the whole suite (upstream PRs #243/#245,
windows-latest, Node 22/24/26; #244/#246 passed on the same code).

Root cause fixed two ways, test-only:
- Generate an EC P-256 (prime256v1) key instead of RSA-2048: constant-time
  keygen with no prime search, so setup is near-instant on every platform.
- Give the before hook its own this.timeout(30000) so one-time cert setup
  never shares the tight per-test budget (belt-and-suspenders).

Node TLS accepts EC self-signed certs, so all assertions and coverage are
unchanged. No lib/, bin/, or dependency changes.

docs: add plan for Windows reverse-mode file unlink flake fix

Diagnosis and decision for the intermittent windows-latest failure in the
"file resources are not available later in reverse mode" api tests: Windows
delete-pending keeps fs.stat succeeding after unlink, so reverse mode rightly
keeps polling; getFileSize already handles EPERM/EBUSY, so it is test
fragility, not a product bug. Fix is test-only headroom + retry.

test: harden Windows reverse-mode file unlink tests against delete-pending flake

On Windows an unlinked file can linger in a delete-pending state: an antivirus
or Search-indexer handle held without FILE_SHARE_DELETE makes Node fall back to
delete-on-close. While pending, fs.stat keeps succeeding and returns the real
size, so reverse mode correctly keeps polling until the OS finishes the delete.
Under load that window exceeds the api suite's this.timeout(3000), so the "file
resources are not available later in reverse mode" tests time out intermittently
(jeffbski/wait-on#238, windows-latest Node 26.x).

getFileSize already maps any fstat error (EPERM/EBUSY/ENOENT) to -1, so the
error-code path is handled in product code; this is test fragility, not a bug.

Give both the callback- and promise-form twins real headroom (this.timeout
15000) and retry with fresh temp files (this.retries(2)), mirroring the repo's
existing Windows-flake handling. Test-only; no lib or dependency changes.

fix: normalize proxy URL and let auth override Authorization header

Two axios→fetch config-parity fixes with full scenario coverage.

B1 — proxy dispatcher construction:
- Bracket a bare IPv6 proxy host (`::1` -> `[::1]`) and strip a trailing
  colon from `proxy.protocol` (`'http:'` -> `'http'`) so proxy objects axios
  normalized build a valid undici URL instead of throwing `Invalid URL`.
- Wrap dispatcher construction in `createHTTP$` so any residual error reaches
  the callback/promise instead of throwing synchronously out of `waitOn()`
  (the API contract, asserted by the malformed-proxy test).

B2 — auth header:
- `opts.auth` now strips any case-variant `Authorization` from `headers`
  before setting Basic, so auth overrides a caller's custom header instead of
  undici comma-merging them.
- Build Basic for partial/empty auth too (each side defaults to ''), matching
  axios's `Basic base64(user:pass)`.

refactor: drop lodash for native equivalents

Replace the eight lodash/fp helpers used in lib/wait-on.js with small
native equivalents and remove the lodash dependency:

- noop            -> () => {}
- once            -> local closure guarding a single invocation
- negate(isBoolean) -> (x) => typeof x !== 'boolean'
- negate(isEmpty)   -> (arr) => arr.length > 0 (only ever called with arrays)
- partial(fn, [deps]) -> arrow closures binding the deps argument
- zip(resources, states) -> resources.map((r, i) => [r, states[i]])
  (combineLatest guarantees equal length, so longest-array padding is moot)
- pick(['ca','cert','key','passphrase'], opts) -> destructure; buildDispatcher
  already guards each with `!== undefined`, so omitted-vs-undefined is identical

No behavior change. The existing suite is the parity bar (144 passing); the
http/https/proxy tests exercise the former pick/buildDispatcher path and every
run exercises once/noop/partial/zip.
